# Recreation Prompt

Create a browser-native, portrait-first canvas action survival game titled **Vice Grid: Heatline Hustle**. Preserve the mechanics of a drag-to-move arena survivor: the player steers a central avatar with touch or mouse, an orbiting automatic attack damages nearby enemies, enemies spawn from screen edges and chase or shoot, defeated enemies award score/kills and may drop upgrades, every ten kills raises heat level, thirty kills spawns a boss, health reaching zero causes failure, and defeating the boss causes victory.

Reinterpret the game through this prompt: Grand Theft Auto open-city action. A Grand Theft Auto open-city action game with urban sandbox freedom, crime chaos, vehicle chases, satire, police pursuit, street-level ambition, dark humor, and open-world systemic mischief with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The focal actor is a neon getaway car in a satirical open-city crime chase. Chasers are patrol cars, bike units, drones, and armored vans. Loot is street upgrades: side-swipe damage, turbo speed, armor, and repair. The boss is a police helicopter called Metro Hawk. Use procedural CSS/canvas art, mobile-readable HUD vocabulary, bold cyan/magenta/amber palette roles, and scoped touch handling so UI buttons stay tappable.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: portrait canvas survival/action arena with light RPG upgrade progression.
- objective: drag the central avatar around the playfield, survive enemy waves, defeat spawned enemies with an automatic orbiting weapon, collect upgrades, trigger a boss after 30 kills, and defeat that boss for victory.
- input model: mouse/touch down and drag on the canvas; the avatar moves toward the current pointer while UI buttons use native click/tap.
- core loop: start run, move continuously, enemies spawn from edges and chase or shoot, orbiting weapon damages enemies, defeated enemies grant score/kills and sometimes loot, every 10 kills raises level, 30 kills spawns a boss, boss defeat wins.
- fail/friction state: contact damage and projectiles reduce health; health at or below zero ends the run and exposes a restart overlay.

## Protected mechanics
- Drag-anywhere canvas movement, speed values, boundary clamping, and pointer/touch semantics.
- Enemy spawn cadence, edge spawning, chaser/erratic/tank/shooter behaviors, contact damage, projectile behavior, and collision radii.
- Orbiting automatic weapon timing, damage application, knockback, and upgrade scaling.
- Score, kill count, level increments every 10 kills, loot drop probability, upgrade effects, boss trigger at 30 kills, win/loss/restart state flow.
- Mobile portrait canvas loop and native button click/tap lifecycle.

## Remixed target
Vice Grid: Heatline Hustle reframes the same survival arena as a satirical portrait open-city getaway chase. The hero becomes a neon getaway car; orbiting weapon becomes a side-swipe ram; enemies become patrol cars, bike units, armored vans, and ticket drones; loot becomes street upgrades; the boss becomes a police helicopter pursuit unit. Mechanics stay intact while the HUD, procedural city, focal silhouette, copy, typography, palette, feedback, and mobile presentation become urban-crime action.
